undefined Isham Dickson (I.D.) Brown,Sr. (youngest son of Felix Brown - My Great Grandfather)
I do not know the correct spelling for Isham although when asked by the Census Taker he said he was Isum Brown (For I am a Brown). He is listed as Dickson Brown on the 1870 MS. census in Felix Brown household.

......6 I.D. Brown, Sr. b. Sept. 1861 at Rials Creek - Mendenhall, Mississippi d. May 15, 1925 Cade, Texas. Buried Wortham Cem. Wortham, TX.
......+ 1st. wife, Lacy Ann Williamson on Sept. 4, 1879 in Simpson Co. MS. b. Feb. 1844 Weathersby, MS. d. 1918 Cade, TX. Buried Wortham Cem., Wortham, TX. Lacy had two children before she married I.D. (1.) Jessie Robin Williamson b. Sept. 17, 1868 d. April 1, 1965 m. Sarah Lillie Finch on Dec. 11, 1890 b. March 7, 1875 d. Sept. 17, 1962. Buried at Goodwater Cem., Magee, MS. His father was an Indian named ? Youngblood. Jessie was named for his Grandfather Jesse and Uncle Robin Williamson. Robin Williamson signed as witness on marriage bond for Lacy Ann & I.D. Brown to marry.

(2.) Francis Anders (Williamson) Brown b. Nov. 4, 1873 d. Apr. 14, 1941 d/o Solomon "Sol" "Speckle" Brown ( I.D. Brown's brother) & Lacy Ann Williamson ( Francis knew Solomon was her father. Whenever he came to visit, Francis would butcher a chicken and fix his favorite meal - chicken and dumplings.) m. John Luther May b. Jan. 8, 1872 Rankin Co., MS. d. Apr. 18, 1955 Weathersby, MS. Son of William Green May b. May 1st. 1842 Dale Co., AL. s/o Isaac & Abbie May & (Letitia) Lucy Ann Catherine "Kate" Williamson. Kate's parents were Anselum Morgan Williamson & Felcia Ann Irby. John L. May remarried as his death certificate says the informant was Mrs. J.L. May (Blanche Jobe). Buried Macedonia Cem. at Rials Creek, Simpson Co., MS. Her father was one of I.D.'s brothers, Sol "Speckle" Brown.(called "Speckle" because he had red hair and full of freckles.) Her mother, Lacy Ann was the daughter of Jesse Williamson & Charlotte "Lottie" Patterson.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text:
Brother Mercante was born in Weirton, West Virginia on June 27, 1940. He was baptized at the age of 11 and began pioneering when he was 21. A year later, in 1962, he arrived at Brooklyn Bethel to begin what would become a 56-year-long Bethel career. David’s determination to support Kingdom interests was strong from the beginning. For example, in accepting his invitation to serve at Bethel, he wrote to Brother Knorr: “I know this is Jehovah’s organization and anything that is done in it must be done as though Jehovah were personally asking that it be done.” That admirable perspective fueled Brother Mercante’s strong sense of loyalty and work ethic.

David began his Bethel service in the Factory and later served as secretary for Max Larson.  Thereafter, he served for decades in the offices supporting the work of Brother Knorr and later the Governing Body, where he had the privilege of assisting many responsible brothers in their weighty assignments. In 2011, Brother Mercante transferred to the Maintenance Department, where he faithfully worked with safety and training.

Brother Mercante found great joy in his assignments. For example, while serving as a zone overseer, he had the opportunity to travel the globe to far-flung places like Sri Lanka, Australia, and West Africa and see firsthand the growth of the brotherhood. David often recounted these experiences with a gleaming smile. His friendliness and warmth could lighten the mood of any gathering.
The apostle Paul said of his fellow workers: “I thank my God always when I remember you…because of the contribution you have made to the good news from the first day until this moment.” (Philippians 1:3, 5) We join the Mercante family in mourning the loss of David. However, like Paul, we also thank Jehovah for having known such a hardworking and lovable brother, and we look forward to seeing him again very soon.

sections.text:
George Edward Sunderland1,2
M, b. 20 February 1903, d. 14 March 1973
Father	John Alvin Sunderland1 b. 10 Jun 1876, d. 1951
Mother	Grace Belle Shafer b. 3 Feb 1884, d. 31 May 1972
Last Edited	6 Jan 2012
Birth*	George Edward Sunderland was born on 20 February 1903 at Worthington, Franklin, Ohio.1,3,4 
(Witness) Census	He appeared on the census of 15 April 1910 Sharon Twp., Franklin, Ohio, in the household of John Alvin Sunderland; ED 197, Sheet 6A, page 283, occupation railroad laborer, renting, married, no wife present, four children.1 
(Witness) Census	George Edward Sunderland appeared on the census of 5 May 1910 Sharon Twp., Franklin, Ohio, in the household of John Alvin Sunderland and Grace Belle Shafer; ED 196, sheet 11A, occupation laborer-street railway, renting, married 10 years, 5 children, 5 living; Grace and Jim are present here but do not appear in the April 15 entry.1 
(Witness) Census	George Edward Sunderland appeared on the census of 1916 Hillcrest, Barth River District 32, Alberta, Canada, in the household of John Alvin Sunderland; District 8B, page 14, occupation farmer, listed as widowed, 4 children.5 
Marriage*	George Edward Sunderland married Nora Lewis Muncie on 16 January 1926 at Franklin, Ohio; by Rev. A.H. Knipping.6,2,4 
Census*	George Edward Sunderland appeared on the census of 16 April 1930 at Sharon Twp., Franklin, OHio, ED 215, sheet 3A, occupation laborer-golf course, owned home valued at $1,000, radio, 3 children at home.6 
Residence*	He lived on 4 December 1936 at 261 Rosslyn Avenue, Worthington, Franklin, Ohio; worked at Northwest Coal Co., located at 942 W. 3rd Ave., Columbus.3 
Marriage*	He married Mary (Maria) C. Crnac between 1962 and 1972.7 
Death*	George Edward Sunderland died on 14 March 1973 at Columbus, Franklin, Ohio, at age 70; buried at the Walnut Grove Cemetery.8,9,10 
Obit	George Edward's obituary was published in the Columbus Dispatch on 15 March 1973:

George E. Sunderland, age 70, 261 Rosslyn Ave. Wednesday at home. Retired contractor. Survived by wife, Mary; sons, Willis W. and Raymond E. Sunderland, both of Worthington; daughter, Mrs. John (Marie) O'Brien of Powell; 11 grandchildren; brothers Stanford Sunderland, Alberta, Canada, James Sunderland, Milton, Fla; sisters, Mrs. John (Nellie) Kuminski and Mrs. Charles (Edna) Wagner, both of Alberta, Canada, Mrs. Ben (Midge) Long, Cols., O; many nieces and nephews. Funeral service 11:30 a.m. Sat., Rev. Roger Bixler officiating. Burial Walnut Grove Cemetery. [Columbus Dispatch, Thursday, March 15, 1973, p. 31A]11 
(Witness) Obit	He witnessed the Obit of Mary (Maria) C. Crnac on 15 May 2001 at Columbus Dispatch, Columbus, Franklin, Ohio,
SUNDERLAND Mary (Maria) C. Sunderland, age 79, Saturday, May 12, 2001 at The Laurels of Norworth. Mary was a member of Our Lady of Peace Catholic Church. Preceded in death by her husband George E. Sunderland; brother Antonio Crnac of Croatia. She is survived by George's family, Marie (John) O'Brien of Powell, Raymond (Zella) Sunderland, and Willis (Dorothy) Sunderland of Worthington; family in Croatia, Giovanni Crnac, Angela, Anna (Giuseppe) Zlatic of Umago; and many friends. Friends may call Tuesday 5-8.7

Data submitted by Janet Howard.  Thank you Janet!


Generation No. 1

1. JAMES T.2 TYRER (TYRER1) (Source: Tami Wheat.) was born 1754 in Devonshire, England, and died 23 Jul 1793 in Wendell, Hampshire Co., MA.. He married RUTH GOODELL 13 Dec 1779 in Hampshire City, Wendell, Massachusetts, daughter of JONATHAN GOODALE and BETSY. She was born 1759 in Hampshire City, Wendell, MA., and died Unknown in Hampshire City, Wendell, MA..

Notes for JAMES T. TYRER:
Source: The records of Congregational Church of Wendell, Mass.
James Tyrer was with Major General John Burgoyne, of the British Army as a Officer. 
Note:
See Attached- Articles of Convention of Saratoga.
See attached-Panning Burgoyne's Offensive: May 1776-May 1777.
See Attached-Summery
See Attached-Burgoyne's Offensive Saratoga Campaign 1777.
See Attached-Aftermath.
See Attached-1777 Time line.
When his regiment surrendered they were cared for in the homes of the Americans. It is said James stayed in the home of Captain Ebeneezer Goodell and this is were he met and married the Captains daughter, Ruth Goodell or Goodall. Spelling not confirmed.
The prisoners were marched to Montreal Canada near Harvard University, then to VA, USA. Some escaped.

Notes for ASA TYRER:
He first came from New York to Illinois 1818. Later with other miners, he would spend summer mining seasons in the vicinity of Dodgeville, Wisconsin and winters in Quincy, IL. 

Asa was not actually a doctor, although he and his wife Chloe are credited with savings many lives in Dodgeville during the great cholera epidemic of the 1850's.

Doctor and coroner may not really apply to him as, handing out whisky-based remedies for cholera may have qualified for many lay minds.

Notes for JAMES DIEGHTON TYRER:
When quite small his parents moved to Wisconsin, where in the mining region they remained for eighteen years, when they moved back to Quincy, Illinois. His father was among the original settlers of Quincy and settled there among the Indians. His father bought a soldier's claim lying adjacent to what is now the city of Quincy. 

Although not a graduate of a medical institute he acquired considerable knowledge, as a physician. James set up his medical practice in 1855. He received a liberal education in Quincy. In 1859 graduated from the Chicago Medical College, and became a prominent citizen of Quincy. He set up and had in running order the first mill stones ever brought to Adams County. James moved and his family moved from Quincy to MT. Sterling, then to Jacksonville and then to Astoria and finally to Marbletown.

sections.text:
George Edward Sunderland1,2
M, b. 20 February 1903, d. 14 March 1973
Father	John Alvin Sunderland1 b. 10 Jun 1876, d. 1951
Mother	Grace Belle Shafer b. 3 Feb 1884, d. 31 May 1972
Last Edited	6 Jan 2012
Birth*	George Edward Sunderland was born on 20 February 1903 at Worthington, Franklin, Ohio.1,3,4 
(Witness) Census	He appeared on the census of 15 April 1910 Sharon Twp., Franklin, Ohio, in the household of John Alvin Sunderland; ED 197, Sheet 6A, page 283, occupation railroad laborer, renting, married, no wife present, four children.1 
(Witness) Census	George Edward Sunderland appeared on the census of 5 May 1910 Sharon Twp., Franklin, Ohio, in the household of John Alvin Sunderland and Grace Belle Shafer; ED 196, sheet 11A, occupation laborer-street railway, renting, married 10 years, 5 children, 5 living; Grace and Jim are present here but do not appear in the April 15 entry.1 
(Witness) Census	George Edward Sunderland appeared on the census of 1916 Hillcrest, Barth River District 32, Alberta, Canada, in the household of John Alvin Sunderland; District 8B, page 14, occupation farmer, listed as widowed, 4 children.5 
Marriage*	George Edward Sunderland married Nora Lewis Muncie on 16 January 1926 at Franklin, Ohio; by Rev. A.H. Knipping.6,2,4 
Census*	George Edward Sunderland appeared on the census of 16 April 1930 at Sharon Twp., Franklin, OHio, ED 215, sheet 3A, occupation laborer-golf course, owned home valued at $1,000, radio, 3 children at home.6 
Residence*	He lived on 4 December 1936 at 261 Rosslyn Avenue, Worthington, Franklin, Ohio; worked at Northwest Coal Co., located at 942 W. 3rd Ave., Columbus.3 
Marriage*	He married Mary (Maria) C. Crnac between 1962 and 1972.7 
Death*	George Edward Sunderland died on 14 March 1973 at Columbus, Franklin, Ohio, at age 70; buried at the Walnut Grove Cemetery.8,9,10 
Obit	George Edward's obituary was published in the Columbus Dispatch on 15 March 1973:

George E. Sunderland, age 70, 261 Rosslyn Ave. Wednesday at home. Retired contractor. Survived by wife, Mary; sons, Willis W. and Raymond E. Sunderland, both of Worthington; daughter, Mrs. John (Marie) O'Brien of Powell; 11 grandchildren; brothers Stanford Sunderland, Alberta, Canada, James Sunderland, Milton, Fla; sisters, Mrs. John (Nellie) Kuminski and Mrs. Charles (Edna) Wagner, both of Alberta, Canada, Mrs. Ben (Midge) Long, Cols., O; many nieces and nephews. Funeral service 11:30 a.m. Sat., Rev. Roger Bixler officiating. Burial Walnut Grove Cemetery. [Columbus Dispatch, Thursday, March 15, 1973, p. 31A]11 
(Witness) Obit	He witnessed the Obit of Mary (Maria) C. Crnac on 15 May 2001 at Columbus Dispatch, Columbus, Franklin, Ohio,
SUNDERLAND Mary (Maria) C. Sunderland, age 79, Saturday, May 12, 2001 at The Laurels of Norworth. Mary was a member of Our Lady of Peace Catholic Church. Preceded in death by her husband George E. Sunderland; brother Antonio Crnac of Croatia. She is survived by George's family, Marie (John) O'Brien of Powell, Raymond (Zella) Sunderland, and Willis (Dorothy) Sunderland of Worthington; family in Croatia, Giovanni Crnac, Angela, Anna (Giuseppe) Zlatic of Umago; and many friends. Friends may call Tuesday 5-8.7
